Commentary.Commentary: …THE RUN CHASE…

England Women were far from their best with the ball and in the field. Lauren Bell stood out with figures of 3/27, proving to be the pick of the bowlers for the home side. However, both Em Arlott and Sophie Ecclestone managed just one wicket each and were a bit expensive. Chasing 211, England will need a standout performance with the bat if they're to take an early lead in the series. Can they rise to the challenge, or will the visitors hold their nerve? Stay tuned — the chase begins shortly.

India Women produced a commanding batting performance to post a formidable total of 210/5 in their 20 overs after being put in to bat first. The openers got off to a flying start, with a solid 77-run stand setting the platform. Shafali Verma contributed a quick 20 before falling, but Smriti Mandhana anchored the innings brilliantly. Mandhana, in sublime touch, combined with Harleen Deol for a rapid 94-run partnership. Deol played a brisk cameo of 43, while Mandhana went on to register her maiden T20I century—a milestone innings that powered India forward. Late fireworks from Richa Ghosh and Deepti Sharma added crucial runs in the death overs, propelling India to an imposing total that is well above par.
A couple to end the innings! Flatter, around off. Deepti Sharma mistimes the pull toward square leg, and they scamper for the double. India Women finish on a mammoth score of 210/5.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now. The teams and the umpires are in the middle. The players offer a minute's silence for the recent airplane tragedy that happened in Ahmedabad. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma will open the innings for India Women. Smriti Mandhana, the India Women's stand-in skipper, says that Harmanpreet Kaur misses out due to a hand injury and is expected to be alright in a few days. Adds that the preparation has been brilliant as they arrived seven to eight days ago. Mentions that they played a few practice matches and had good net sessions. Closes by sharing that Shree Charani makes her T20I debut today.

Nat Sciver-Brunt, the England Women skipper, wins the toss and opts to bowl. Says that it looks a good wicket and she has played a lot of cricket here. Adds that she is just excited to get going today, and they have a heavy pace attack today.

With world-class players on both sides and plenty to play for, we’re set for a gripping contest. So, who will draw first blood and go 1-0 up in the series? Stick with us for the toss and team news coming up shortly!

India Women, on the other hand, are playing their first T20I series of 2025. They come off a successful home series win against West Indies Women and have had a well-earned break following a demanding tri-series in Sri Lanka in May. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur will lead a batting unit anchored by Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues, with the explosive Shafali Verma returning to the XI after a brief absence. The middle and lower order will rely on the firepower of Richa Ghosh, Amanjot Kaur, and Deepti Sharma, while Shree Charani and Kranti Goud are exciting talents to watch.

The home side, England Women, enter the series brimming with confidence after a dominant whitewash against West Indies Women. Nat Sciver-Brunt has settled well into her leadership role, while seasoned campaigners like Danielle Wyatt-Hodge, Sophia Dunkley, Sophie Ecclestone, and Lauren Bell remain central to their success. Promising youngsters such as Em Arlott, Alice Capsey, Linsey Smith, and Issy Wong have impressed in recent outings and continue to rise through the ranks. England, with both form and familiarity on their side, will start the series as favourites.

Hello, and a warm welcome to our coverage of the first T20I in the five-match series between India Women and England Women, from Trent Bridge in Nottingham. With the T20 World Cup just a year away in similar English conditions, this series offers a perfect platform for both sides to experiment with new players and strategies as they gear up for the marquee event.
…MATCHDAY…

The international cricket calendar shows no signs of slowing down, and we’re all the better for it. Amid a packed global schedule featuring men’s Tests, T20 leagues, and domestic showdowns, women’s cricket is set to take centre stage as India Women gear up for an exciting tour of England. The tour features five T20Is followed by three ODIs, promising a riveting white-ball contest between two top-tier sides. With the men of both nations already battling it out in whites, it’s now over to the women to light up the English summer with skill, flair, and fierce competition in this all white-ball series. This marks England Women’s third white ball series, and the second home series this year. After a winless women’s Ashes in January, England Women bounced back in fine fashion against West Indies Women on home soil, where they executed the clean sweep in both white ball formats. This series carries far more weight than just bilateral bragging rights. It’s a pivotal tune-up for the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, set to be hosted in England next year. With five T20Is on the cards, this offers both teams a golden opportunity to fine-tune combinations, test bench strength, and adapt to the conditions that will mirror the World Cup stage. For India, it’s their first T20I assignment of the year and a chance to reset after a very turbulent 2024 campaign, as the tour doubles as a strategic reconnaissance mission. England have named a strong 14-player squad for this T20I series, and it comes with a few notable changes and comebacks. The headline is the return of star spinner Sophie Ecclestone, who rejoins the side after a short break to manage a quad issue and focus on her well-being. Her comeback adds significant firepower to England’s spin department, but it also means leg-spinner Sarah Glenn misses out, a tough call given the depth in England’s spin stocks. There’s also a forced change with former skipper Heather Knight ruled out due to a hamstring injury sustained during the West Indies series. Durham's fast bowler Lauren Filer steps in as her replacement, adding pace and variety to the bowling attack. Led by Natalie Sciver-Brunt, the squad otherwise retains the core that swept the West Indies 3-0, with head coach Charlotte Edwards emphasizing continuity and readiness ahead of the main event at home next year. India have a packed T20I calendar leading up to the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup, with this England tour marking the start of a crucial preparation phase. While they’re set to play three T20Is at home against Bangladesh, another three in Australia in February 2026, and a high-stakes tri-series in New Zealand alongside England in May, this upcoming series offers something distinct, which is an early opportunity to test new faces in English conditions. Shafali Verma is set to reclaim her spot at the top of the order, riding high on strong domestic and WPL form. During her absence in the West Indies T20Is, Uma Chetry partnered Smriti Mandhana but couldn’t make a mark. India’s bowling unit sees a fresh injection of talent, with maiden T20I call-ups for left-arm spinner Shree Charani and seam-bowling all-rounders Kranti Gaud and Sayali Satghare. Amanjot Kaur returns to the squad, while Sneh Rana makes her T20I comeback after over two years, buoyed by standout performances in WPL 2025 and a solid showing in the tour game against ECB XI. She will be a key spinner in ranks, partnering the likes of vastly experienced Deepti Sharma. With Renuka Singh and Pooja Vastrakar sidelined due to injuries, India’s pace attack looks inexperienced. Only Radha Yadav remains from the December T20Is, making this series a key opportunity to test and build depth ahead of their return. India head into the series with a power-packed batting lineup, featuring stalwarts like Harmanpreet Kaur, Smriti Mandhana, Harleen Deol, and Jemimah Rodrigues. However, the spotlight will be on their inexperienced bowling attack as they take on a formidable English side that thrives on home soil. The last tour in 2023 ended in a stinging 3-0 whitewash for India, adding an extra edge to their quest for redemption. The white-ball series kicks off at Trent Bridge, Nottingham, and winds through England, concluding at Chester-le-Street with the ODIs, setting the stage for an enthralling white ball contest between two fierce rivals.
